## Findings

1. **F1 — Creation and readiness are described incorrectly.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:225) says new issues start `backlog` and that prechecks gate `ready`; `issue create` creates dependency-free issues as `Ready`, and gates do not block `Ready`. Remediate the diagrams and prose to describe the actual initial `Ready` state and prechecks at `Ready → InProgress`.

2. **F2 — Gate status calls the actual `pending` state “required.”** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:523) and [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:578) document `required/passed/failed`; the serialized enum is `pending/passed/failed`. Remediate the state diagram and status text to use `pending`.

3. **F3 — Documentation says automatic gate evaluation completes an issue, but it does not.** [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:1366), [custom-gates.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/custom-gates.md:549), [software-development.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/software-development.md:200), [overview.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/overview.md:134), and [troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:54) claim postchecks run on `issue update --state done` and/or the last automated gate auto-transitions `gated → done`. That command only checks statuses and diverts to `Gated`; automatic `gate evaluate` returns after recording its run. Remediate with the actual explicit evaluation/retry workflow and distinguish manual-gate auto-transition behavior.

4. **F4 — Failed prechecks are said to move an issue to `gated`.** [custom-gates.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/custom-gates.md:517) says a failed precheck gates the issue; the handler returns a transition-blocked error and leaves it `Ready`. Remediate the failure-path explanation.

5. **F5 — Type labels are falsely documented as universally required.** [labels.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/labels.md:224), [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:834), [example-config.toml](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/example-config.toml:119), and [custom-gates.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/custom-gates.md:904) say every issue has exactly one `type:*` label or emits a missing-type warning. A type is only defaulted when `[validation].default_type` is configured; the rules enforce at most one, not requiredness. Remediate all such claims, including the incorrect `--orphan` exception.

6. **F6 — `issue assign` is documented as a lifecycle transition.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:728) and [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:763) say `Ready` is necessarily unassigned and `issue assign` moves it to `InProgress`. Assignment only changes the assignee; `issue claim` is the command that promotes a ready issue. Remediate the state and command descriptions.

7. **F7 — `issue claim` and `claim-next` are falsely described as atomic exclusive coordination.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:1074), [quickstart.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/quickstart.md:23), and [first-workflow.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/first-workflow.md:327) describe them as race-safe. They read candidates/assignment before separate writes; only `jit claim acquire` holds the exclusive claims lock. Remediate multi-agent guidance to use advisory leases for exclusivity.

8. **F8 — `issue claim-next --filter` is advertised as functional but its handler ignores the filter.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:949) and [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:1105) promise filtered selection. Remediate by removing filter-based examples until that behavior exists.

9. **F9 — The documented restricted, terminal state machine is not enforced.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:734), [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:754), and [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:966) say Done/Rejected cannot return to active states or transition to each other. Non-`Done` target states are accepted by the update/reject paths. Remediate the diagrams and terminal-state claims to match actual guards.

10. **F10 — A documented bulk-update command is invalid.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:957) combines an issue ID with `--filter`, but clap marks them mutually exclusive. Remediate by removing `abc123` or replacing `--filter` with a single-issue update.

11. **F11 — Two `jq` examples omit the required leading dot.** [design-philosophy.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/design-philosophy.md:264) and [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:1158) use `issues[0].id` and `id`. Remediate to `.issues[0].id` and `.id`.

12. **F12 — Atomic-write guarantees over-credit rename and misstate the implementation.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:59) and [design-philosophy.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/design-philosophy.md:69) say all writes use the shown temp-file/rename pattern and that rename prevents races. Event writes are locked append operations, and locks—not rename—serialize read/modify/write coordination. Remediate the guarantee and remove the stale pseudo-implementation.

13. **F13 — Event-log guarantees are overstated and the declared “full” event list is stale.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:121) says every mutation is logged, [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:125) omits current event variants, and [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:155) says timestamps establish causal ordering. Remediate to the actual state-change invariant, cite the event enum for the current set, and remove the causal-ordering claim.

14. **F14 — The invariant count is obsolete.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:10) claims four invariants and three registered ones; `.jit/invariants.toml` currently registers nine. Remediate by citing the registry without maintaining a count.

15. **F15 — `jit doc archive` is incorrectly listed as requiring Git.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:199) contradicts the filesystem-based archive handler. Remediate by removing it from the Git-required list.

16. **F16 — Qualified item-ID grammar is incomplete.** [cli-command-grammar.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-command-grammar.md:98) gives `<scope>/<self-id>`, omitting the required kind segment. Remediate with `@/<kind>/<self-id>`, `@/issue/<issue-ref>/<kind>/<self-id>`, and the documented issue sugar form.

17. **F17 — A dependency-removal script treats dependency IDs as objects.** [dependency-management.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/dependency-management.md:617) uses `.dependencies[].id`, but dependencies serialize as UUID strings. Remediate to `.dependencies[]`.

18. **F18 — Graph root/leaf direction is reversed.** [dependency-management.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/dependency-management.md:359) says no incoming edges means a root that can start, and no outgoing edges means a leaf with no dependencies. `graph roots` selects issues whose dependency lists are empty. Remediate the graph-reading guidance to match the documented `FROM depends on TO` edge direction.

19. **F19 — Runtime configuration documentation advertises inactive controls.** [configuration.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/configuration.md:229), [configuration.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/configuration.md:274), [configuration.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/configuration.md:302), and [configuration.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/configuration.md:338) present worktree mode, lease timing/renewal, global-operation, lock, and event fields as runtime controls. Current handlers only consume the indefinite-lease limits; worktree mode and the listed timing/event controls are parsed/displayed but not applied. Agent `auto_heartbeat` is also documented as default-true despite defaulting false and having no runner. Remediate the reference and related coordination examples to document only active behavior.

20. **F20 — Repo-local type values are presented as generic shipped configuration.** [README.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/README.md:229), [configuration.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/configuration.md:60), [storage-format.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/storage-format.md:152), and [example-config.toml](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/example-config.toml:44) add `bug`/`enhancement` without saying these are this repository’s dogfood choices. Remediate by using only shipped defaults or clearly framing the snippets as this repository’s configuration.

21. **F21 — The dogfooding transcript is stale current-state narration with rotting counts.** [design-philosophy.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/design-philosophy.md:367) through [line 445](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/design-philosophy.md:445) presents historical issue totals, IDs, statuses, gates, and “Will pass” output as current. Remediate by replacing it with timeless examples or live commands without captured project-state assertions.

22. **F22 — Scope documentation falsely says JIT does not run builds.** [scope.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/scope.md:210) contradicts automated gate checkers, which execute configured commands such as build/test tools. Remediate to say JIT is not a CI system while acknowledging that gate checkers run local commands.

23. **F23 — The development Web UI setup cannot reach the API as described.** [deployment.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/deployment.md:21) says Vite connects to `jit-server`; this repository’s Vite configuration has no `/api` proxy. Remediate to use `jit-server --web-dir web/dist` or a configured reverse proxy.

24. **F24 — The Docker Compose quick start omits required initialization.** [deployment.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/deployment.md:83) starts services against a new volume, but `jit-server` refuses an uninitialized data directory. Remediate by initializing the shared volume with the CLI before `docker compose up`.

25. **F25 — The server data-directory default is incorrect.** [deployment.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/deployment.md:133) says `JIT_DATA_DIR` defaults to `/data`; `jit-server` defaults to `./.jit`, while Docker sets `/data` explicitly. Remediate the table to distinguish native default from Docker configuration.

26. **F26 — Troubleshooting says `jit status` regenerates worktree identity.** [troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:341) is false; status only reads issue storage. Remediate by using an identity-creating claim or worktree command.

27. **F27 — Troubleshooting attributes secondary-worktree visibility to `worktree.mode`.** [troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:347) through [line 369](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:369) instructs users to toggle a mode that current reads do not consult. Remediate with the actual Git/index/main-worktree fallback prerequisites.

28. **F28 — Troubleshooting directs claims-index and stale-lock repair to `jit validate --fix`.** [troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:213) through [line 230](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:230) conflicts with the documented and implemented separation: `jit recover` repairs coordination state. Remediate the recovery sequence to use `jit recover`.
